Senses.Note: The headword spans ordinary spatial reference, comparisons, verse imagery, questions, and compounds. The curated witnesses foreground recurrent Chan deployment rather than the hundreds of scholastic similes in one prolific compilation. The exact graph pair remains "empty space" even where English idiom favors "sky."

Occurrences.Kwic: 此一瓣香虛空包不住。大地載不起。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (天目中峰廣錄): Zhongfeng Mingben is the exact speaker. Extensive Record of Zhongfeng Mingben (天目中峰廣錄), spoken by Zhongfeng Mingben: this one petal of incense cannot be contained by empty space or supported by the great earth.
Source text (蔗菴範禪師語錄): Zhe'an Fan is the exact speaker. Recorded Sayings of Zhe'an Fan (蔗菴範禪師語錄), spoken by Zhe'an Fan: if understood here, empty space can be measured.

Occurrences.Kwic: 舉頭頓忘迷悟如虛空玲瓏不可湊泊
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text Memorial Collection (林間錄): the compiler of the memorial record narrates Cao Benrong’s experience and describes him suddenly forgetting delusion and awakening, with empty space lucid and impossible to grasp; Cao does not utter the comparison. Source title: (普濟玉琳國師語錄).

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: The unquoted memorial sentence predicates the experience of Cao Benrong in biography.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師云：「待虛空粉碎來向汝道。」云：「粉碎後如何？」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (古雪哲禪師語錄): Guxue Zhe is the exact speaker. Recorded Sayings of Guxue Zhe (古雪哲禪師語錄), public exchange: Guxue Zhe postpones his answer until empty space shatters, and the monk asks what follows.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師云。一棒打破虛空。進云。過在什麼處。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (圓悟佛果禪師語錄): Yuanwu Keqin is the exact speaker. Recorded Sayings of Yuanwu Foguo (圓悟佛果禪師語錄): Yuanwu Keqin answers a request for the upward road with one blow that breaks empty space; the questioner asks where the fault lies.

Occurrences.Kwic: 虛空無內外，心法亦如是。若了虛空故，是達真如理。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (祖堂集): Buddhanandi is the exact speaker. Patriarchs' Hall Collection (祖堂集), explicit biography of Buddhanandi: Buddhanandi's transmitted verse says empty space has no inside or outside and compares mind and teaching to it.

Occurrences.Kwic: 莫向虛空裏釘橛有一屠兒身上常出乳香舍利
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (古尊宿語錄): Foyan Qingyuan is the exact speaker. Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄), Foyan Qingyuan's room instruction: Foyan Qingyuan warns against driving a stake into empty space before introducing the butcher account.

Occurrences.Kwic: 你若揀辨，大似虛空中畫疆界；你若不揀辨，又是漆桶裏坐墨煤。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (雪關禪師語錄): Xueguan Zhiyin is the exact speaker. Recorded Sayings of Xueguan Zhiyin (雪關禪師語錄), section on muddled Chan: Xueguan Zhiyin compares discriminating to drawing boundaries in empty space, then gives the contrary warning.

Occurrences.Kwic: 眾請偈，師不荅。將二鼓，復索筆書曰：一燈在望，更無言說。大地平沉，虛空迸裂。書畢，泊然而寂。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (續燈存稿): Longji Youyun Zongmao is the exact speaker. Surviving Draft of the Continued Lamp (續燈存稿), biography of Longji Youyun Zongmao: Longji writes a final verse in which the great earth sinks and empty space bursts apart, then dies.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂：達磨正宗，衲僧巴鼻。充塞虛空，無處回避。堪笑迷流，白日青天開却眼，只管瞌睡。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (續燈存稿): Wuchu Daguan is the exact speaker. Surviving Draft of the Continued Lamp (續燈存稿), biography of Wuchu Daguan: Wuchu Daguan says Bodhidharma's true lineage fills empty space with nowhere to evade it.

Senses.Explanation: Empty space is the open expanse in which things can be located or compared. The term is attested 5,943 times in 279 allowlisted texts. Chan records also make that ordinary expanse measurable, containable, breakable, and fillable. Productive forms include "in empty space" (虛空中, 90 occurrences), "inside empty space" (虛空裏, 136), and "like empty space" (如虛空, 364). They also record impossible or emphatic actions: "empty space shattered" (虛空粉碎, 167), "break empty space" (打破虛空, 85), and "empty space burst apart" (虛空迸裂). Zhongfeng says of an incense offering, "empty space cannot contain it; the great earth cannot support it" (虛空包不住，大地載不起). Zhe'an Fan says that if one understands at a stated point, "empty space can be measured" (虛空可量). A memorial narrative describes one who raised his head and suddenly forgot confusion and awakening, "lucid like empty space, impossible to approach or lodge in" (如虛空玲瓏不可湊泊). The corpus also says "empty space has no inside or outside" (虛空無內外, 9), while a formal address says that the Chan lineage's defining feature "fills empty space, with nowhere to evade it" (充塞虛空，無處回避). These are literal comparisons and recorded predicates; no single further sense is imposed on all 5,943 occurrences.
